atia-mosque.desc: Atia Mosque in Delduar upazila was built in 1609 in the early Mughal period. Its brick walls are covered in terracotta panels of flowers and geometric patterns, blending Sultanate and Mughal styles. The building appeared on an old ten-taka banknote, which made it widely known. It stands beside the Louhajang river in a peaceful village setting.
blocks: How to get there
CNG from Tangail town to Atia, about 30 minutes.
Good to know
It is an active mosque; visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
karatia-zamindar-bari.desc: The Panni family, Afghan in origin and the builders of the Atia Mosque, later made Karatia their base. The best-known of them, Wajed Ali Khan Panni, called 'Chand Mia', was a generous zamindar and a fierce opponent of British rule, and in 1926 he founded Saadat College here, one of the oldest colleges in the region. The zamindar house with its old buildings, gates and pond stands beside the college campus. It makes a good pair with Atia Mosque on a Tangail heritage day.
blocks: How to get there
Karatia lies on the Dhaka–Tangail highway a few kilometres before Tangail town; get off any Tangail bus at Karatia and walk or take a rickshaw.
Good to know
Parts of the house may be closed; you can still see the exterior and walk the college grounds.

glance: Kalidas Mistanna Bhandar beside the Dhaka–Tangail highway at Jamurki, Mirzapur (about 20 km before Tangail town)

jamurki-sandesh.desc: Jamurki, a village in Mirzapur upazila on the Dhaka–Tangail highway, is known across the country for its sandesh. The tradition goes back to Madan Mohan Saha in the British period; his son Kalidas Saha made the sandesh famous, and the shop still carries his name. It is made from fresh chhana with sugar or with date-palm gur, and is soft, grainy and fragrant. Jamurki sandesh received Geographical Indication status in 2025.
blocks: Good to know
Easy stop on the way to or from Tangail; buses can drop you at Jamurki.

tangail-saree-weaving.desc: The Tangail sari is a fine cotton or cotton-silk sari woven with bright borders and small woven motifs. Weaving families, many from the Basak community, have worked the looms in villages such as Pathrail in Delduar upazila for generations. You can hear the rhythm of the looms as you walk through the lanes, and many households sell directly from home. Bangladesh registered the Tangail saree as a Geographical Indication in 2024.
blocks: Good to know
Buying directly from weavers in Pathrail usually costs less than in city shops.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
dhanbari-nawab-palace.desc: Dhanbari was the seat of Nawab Syed Nawab Ali Chowdhury, a 19th–20th century zamindar who was among the founders of Dhaka University and an early advocate of Bengali as a state language. His family home, locally called the Nawab Palace or Nawab Manzil, stands beside a large pond and an old mosque, possibly Mughal in origin, that the Nawab enlarged and decorated inside with floral chini-tikri (broken china) mosaic. The family also produced Mohammad Ali of Bogra, a prime minister of Pakistan. The mosque is open for prayer and visitors; the palace is best seen from its grounds.
blocks: How to get there
From Tangail town take a bus toward Madhupur/Dhanbari, then a rickshaw or auto to the Nawab Bari.
Good to know
Combine it with Madhupur forest, which is close by. Ask before entering the palace building.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
nagarpur-zamindar-bari.desc: In Nagarpur upazila stands the palace of the Chowdhury zamindars, an ornate two-storey building with arches, balconies and decorative plasterwork. Parts of the estate now house a college, and the main building has aged gently. It sees far fewer visitors than Mohera, so the mood is quiet. Combine it with a ride through the river country of southern Tangail.
blocks: How to get there
Bus or CNG from Tangail town to Nagarpur, about 1 hour.
Good to know
Ask permission at the college gate if entering the grounds.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
pakutia-zamindar-bari.desc: In the early 1800s the wealthy trader Ramkrishna Saha Mandal came from Calcutta and set up a zamindari at Pakutia, helped by the old steamer link between Nagarpur and Calcutta. In 1915 the family built three palaces of the same design side by side over about 15 acres, known as the 'three mahals'. Each facade is topped by a pair of sculpted female figures framed by flowers and creepers. The buildings are worn and partly in use, and very few tourists make it this far.
blocks: How to get there
From Tangail town or Nagarpur take a CNG or auto to Pakutia; it can also be reached from Saturia in Manikganj.
Good to know
Combine it with Nagarpur Chowdhury Bari. Parts of the buildings are in use, so ask before going inside.

porabari-chomchom.desc: Chomchom from Porabari, a village on the Dhaleshwari just outside Tangail town, is one of the best-known sweets in Bangladesh and holds Geographical Indication status. Made from chhana, it is cooked slowly in syrup until the outside turns brick-red and slightly crisp while the inside stays grainy and juicy. It is often dusted with dried khoa. Many shops in Tangail town sell it, though locals argue over which is closest to the original.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
madhupur-forest.desc: The Madhupur tract is an area of raised red-soil land once covered in sal forest. Part of it is protected as Madhupur National Park, with trails, a watchtower and a rest area near Rasulpur. Garo (Mandi) communities have lived in and around the forest for generations. Early mornings bring birdsong and, with luck, capped langurs in the canopy.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Dhaka or Tangail to Madhupur, then a CNG to the national park entrance at Rasulpur.
Good to know
Hire a local guide for the trails; respect Garo villages and ask before taking photos.

glance: Jalchatra bazar and roadside stalls around Madhupur
madhupur-pineapple.desc: The Madhupur area is one of the country's main pineapple growing regions, with fields stretching across the red-soil land. The local fruit is small, fragrant and very sweet when ripe. In June and July the Jalchatra haat and roadside stalls are piled high. Buy one cut and salted for an instant snack.

madhupur-garo-culture.desc: The Garo, who call themselves Mandi, are one of the indigenous peoples living in and around the Madhupur forest. Their society is matrilineal, with property passing through the mother's line. Many celebrate Wangala, the harvest festival honouring the sun god Saljong, with drums and dance, and Christmas is a major event in the villages. Visiting with a local contact is the respectful way to learn more.
blocks: Good to know
Always ask before photographing people; go with someone who knows the community.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
mohera-zamindar-bari.desc: Mohera Zamindar Bari in Mirzapur upazila is a group of early 20th-century mansions built by a family of wealthy merchants. The buildings are painted in soft colours, with columns, arches and decorative balconies, set around a large pond and gardens. It now houses a police training centre, which is why it is so well maintained, and the grounds are open to visitors. It is one of the most photographed heritage sites near Dhaka.
blocks: How to get there
Bus on the Dhaka–Tangail highway to Natiapara or Mirzapur, then a short auto ride.
Good to know
It is a police facility; follow the rules on where you may walk and photograph.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
hemnagar-zamindar-bari.desc: Zamindar Hemchandra Chowdhury built this two-storey palace in 1890 at Shimlapara mouza, the area now known as Hemnagar, when the Jamuna swallowed his earlier riverside seat at Subarnakhali. Craftsmen from Delhi and Kolkata covered the walls, pillars and gates with flowers, stars and creepers worked in coloured glass, cowrie shells and stone, and two fairy sculptures on the facade gave it the local name Porir Dalan. The estate once had wells, a zoo, an elephant stable, a two-storey theatre hall and a big tank with brick-paved ghats. Much of that is gone and the building is worn, but the facade still makes the trip worthwhile.
blocks: How to get there
From Tangail take a bus to Gopalpur, then a CNG or easy-bike to Hemnagar.
Good to know
Parts of the old building are fragile; don't climb on broken stairs or walls. Morning light is best on the facade.

glance: 80 km to Tangail by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
201-dome-mosque.desc: Completed in 2019 in South Pathalia village of Gopalpur upazila, this mosque is named for its domes: one large central dome ringed by 200 smaller ones. A separate minaret 137 metres high rises beside it and is described as the tallest concrete minaret in the world. The whole Qur'an is inscribed on the west wall, and the prayer hall holds around 15,000 people. It was built by a private welfare trust on the east bank of the Jhenai, and the complex also has an orphanage and a free clinic. It draws day-trippers from all over the country.
blocks: How to get there
From Tangail town take a bus or CNG to Gopalpur, then an auto to South Pathalia (Nagda Simla union).
Good to know
Dress modestly; women should carry a scarf. Avoid Friday midday prayers if you want to look around.
